上計簿徒具文則有責三公不察吏治則
有責其所以振刷綜理者皆未嘗少越於
===
舊法之外惟其實事求是而不參虛聲信
賞必罰而真僞無眩是以當時吏稱其職
民安其業政事文學法理之士咸精其能
下至技巧工匠後世鮮及故崔寔稱其優
於孝文而仲長統極其嘆服荀悅論美元
帝而亭德裕深以爲非良不誣矣然則今
之欲求治理者又奚以紛紛多事爲哉
高皇帝畢智竭慮以定一代之制非如漢祖之
日不暇給也
punctuated:
綜覈之主也。然考其當時所行，則固未嘗新一令、創一制，惟曰取其祖宗之法，修飭而振舉之，如曰「漢家自有制度」耳。且其所任魏相，最為稱上意者，亦未嘗以已意有所論建，惟條奏漢家故事及名臣賈誼、晁錯等言耳。當其時，雖五日一視事，而上下相維，無苟且之意。吏不奉宣詔書則有責，上計簿徒具文則有責，三公不察吏治則有責。其所以振刷綜理者，皆未嘗少越於舊法之外。惟其實事求是而不采虛聲，信賞必罰而真偽無眩，是以當時吏稱其職，民安其業，政事、文學、法理之士咸精其能，下至技巧工匠，後世鮮及。故崔寔稱其優於孝文，而仲長統極其嘆服；荀悅論美元帝，而李德裕深以為非，良不誣矣。然則今之欲求治理者，又奚以紛紛多事為哉？
高皇帝畢智竭慮，以定一代之制，非如漢祖之日不暇給也。
translation_en:
…was a ruler who comprehensively scrutinized affairs. Yet if we examine what he did at the time, he never introduced a new ordinance or created a new institution. He simply took the laws of his ancestors, put them in order, and restored their effective operation—as he said, “The house of Han has its own institutions.” Moreover, Wei Xiang, whom he employed and who best accorded with his wishes, never advanced proposals based on his own ideas, but merely submitted itemized memorials citing Han precedents and the statements of eminent ministers such as Jia Yi and Chao Cuo. At that time, although the emperor attended to business only once every five days, superiors and subordinates kept one another in check, and none approached their duties perfunctorily. Officials were held accountable if they failed to promulgate imperial edicts; they were held accountable if their annual administrative reports were mere formalities; and the Three Dukes were held accountable if they failed to scrutinize local administration. None of the measures by which he reinvigorated and comprehensively managed government departed in the slightest from the established laws. He sought the truth in actual affairs rather than pursuing hollow acclaim, made rewards dependable and punishments certain, and allowed no confusion between the genuine and the false. Thus officials fulfilled their duties, the people pursued their livelihoods in peace, and men versed in government, classical learning, and legal principles all excelled in their abilities. Even the skilled craftsmen of his time were seldom equaled in later ages. Thus Cui Shi judged him superior to Emperor Xiaowen, and Zhongchang Tong expressed the utmost admiration for him. When Xun Yue praised Emperor Yuan in his assessment, Li Deyu emphatically judged him mistaken. These judgments were indeed well founded. Why, then, should those who now seek good government busy themselves with a profusion of undertakings?
Emperor Gao exhausted his wisdom and devoted all his thought to establishing the institutions of a dynasty. His circumstances were unlike those of the Han founder, who could scarcely find enough time each day to meet pressing demands.

===

鄧以讚

===
代則荀卿所謂俗儒也
第三問
鄧以讚
同考試官檢討沈 批〔以英雄豪傑賁慎所養極為〕〔館論亦足占所養矣〕

punctuated:
列聖相承，創守一道，非有武帝之紛更中變也。百官承式，海內嚮風，非有許史霍氏之專制撓法也。成憲具存，舊章森列，明君賢臣相與實圖之而已。毋不事事，毋泰多事，祛積習以作頹靡，振紀綱以正風俗，省議論以定國是，覈名實以行賞罰，則法行如流，而事功輻湊矣。若曰：「此漢事耳，吾且為唐虞，為三代。」則荀卿所謂俗儒也。
第三問
鄧以讚
同考試官檢討沈批：以英雄豪傑貴慎所養，極為確論，亦足占所養矣。
同考試官檢討許批：非常之才，患無所養。覽子策，以養之素矣，他日吾觀其用焉。
同考試官編修李批：評隲往哲，錙銖不爽，篇終歸
translation_en:
The successive sage emperors have inherited the throne, following a single Way in founding and preserving the dynasty; there have been none of Emperor Wu’s incessant alterations and changes of course. The officials all observe the established standards, and all within the seas look to their example; there has been none of the monopolization of power and subversion of law practiced by the Xu, Shi, and Huo families. The established statutes remain fully intact, and the old regulations stand in orderly array. An enlightened ruler and worthy ministers need only work together earnestly to put them into effect. Neither neglect affairs nor undertake excessive initiatives. Eradicate entrenched habits to rouse the dispirited; invigorate discipline to rectify customs; reduce disputation to settle the guiding principles of state; and scrutinize names against realities to administer rewards and punishments. Then the laws will operate as smoothly as flowing water, and achievements will converge like spokes at a hub. If someone says, “These are merely Han practices; I intend instead to emulate Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties,” he is what Master Xun called a vulgar Confucian.

Deng Yizan

text:
蓍蔡不敢以言智懼其算之易窮也力若
九牛不敢以言任懼其趨之易僨也煉之
至精而歛之至密韜之至深而蓄之至厚
夫然後其神凝其氣專發之不可禦索之
不可窮矣人徒見其事業聲稱照燿今古
抑孰測其所以致之者哉今夫兩間清淑
之氣麗於形象在天為星辰在地為河嶽
在土石為寶玉在飛走為麟鳳在人則為
英雄豪傑是英雄豪傑者固均之二氣之
===
間鍾人倫之首出者也然有辨焉劉卲才
云聰明秀出謂之英膽力過人謂之雄有
英而不雄者有雄而不英者智勇並異則
英雄兼焉淮南解曰才過千人謂之豪萬
人謂之傑此英雄豪傑之辨也總之皆以
其智勇殊絕不可以尋常尺度論耳自古
迄今所以樹立人紀恢翊世運决大疑排
大難建大功立大節必此四人者為之然
而品格異焉不可不察也夫人非無才之

…as divining milfoil and tortoise shells, they dare not claim wisdom, fearing that their calculations may readily be exhausted; though as strong as nine oxen, they dare not claim the capacity to bear great responsibilities, fearing that their advance may readily end in a fall. They refine their capacities to the utmost purity and gather them in with the utmost care; they conceal them in the greatest depths and accumulate the richest reserves. Only then does their spirit become concentrated and their vital energy focused: once released, these cannot be resisted; when drawn upon, they cannot be exhausted. People see only their achievements and renown shining through past and present. Yet who can fathom the means by which they attained them?
Now, the pure and auspicious vital energy between Heaven and Earth attaches itself to visible forms. In Heaven it becomes the stars; on earth, rivers and mountains; among soil and stone, precious jade; among flying and running creatures, qilin and phoenixes; and among human beings, brilliant, bold, outstanding, and exceptional men. Such men alike receive a concentration of the two vital energies, yin and yang, making them foremost among humankind [?]. Yet distinctions exist among them. Liu Shao’s discussion of talent [?] states: “Those whose intelligence and discernment stand out are called brilliant (ying); those whose courage and strength surpass others are called bold (xiong).” Some are brilliant but not bold; others are bold but not brilliant. When both wisdom and courage are exceptional, brilliance and boldness are combined. The Explanations of Huainan (Huainan jie) says: “One whose talent surpasses a thousand people is called outstanding (hao); one whose talent surpasses ten thousand is called exceptional (jie).” These are the distinctions among the brilliant, the bold, the outstanding, and the exceptional. In general, all possess such extraordinary wisdom and courage that they cannot be assessed by ordinary measures. From antiquity to the present, it has invariably been these four types of men who have established the guiding principles of human relations, sustained and enlarged the fortunes of their age, resolved great uncertainties, overcome great difficulties, accomplished great deeds, and demonstrated great integrity. title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
患有才而能善用之爲難四人者其機智
勇决既與凡民迥異則未免過於自恃而
有眇焉輕天下之心紛錯未交而謂幾不
足與晰也艱阻未試而謂功不足與圖也
考衷叩蘊則固未有灼然先幾之見確然
不可奪之守一挫其銳則折北而不振矣
是純乎氣者也品之下也夫千鈞之弩不
以鼷鼠發機萬石之鐘不爲尺梃成響物
理有分感應有節不可易也四人者負其
===
才具則不能安於無事往往不勝技癢曲
牽於應世之迹而輕試其所長是以見彈
求鴞或欲速而不達按珠抵鵲或見小而
妨大此與虛憍恃氣者固有間矣然而其
彊可撓也其躁可激也其驕可乘也其欲
可豢也以綜天下之務則得失參焉不可
與謀成也是識不能勝其才者也等而上
焉嚴乎内外審於施應既不沾沾以自喜
亦不汲汲以從時自度其智可與幾也將

…the concern; rather, the difficulty lies in possessing talent and being able to use it well. These four types of men, whose resourcefulness, intelligence, courage, and decisiveness differ so greatly from those of ordinary people, inevitably become excessively self-reliant and look down upon the world with disdain. Before entanglements arise, they declare that incipient developments scarcely warrant their discernment; before encountering hardships, they declare that achievements scarcely warrant their planning. Yet if one examines their hearts and probes what lies within, they possess neither clear insight that anticipates developments nor firm resolve that cannot be shaken. Once their keen edge is blunted, they suffer defeat and cannot recover. Such men are governed entirely by spirit and mettle; theirs is the lowest grade.
Now, a crossbow with a draw weight of a thousand jun is not discharged at a tiny mouse; a bell weighing ten thousand shi is not made to ring by a stick a foot long. Things have their proper capacities, and stimulus and response have their due limits: these cannot be altered. Relying on their talents, these four types of men cannot rest content when there is nothing to do. Often unable to resist the itch to display their skills, they become unduly entangled in the outward activities of engaging with the world and lightly put their strengths to the test. Thus, seeing a pellet, they seek an owl [?], sometimes failing to attain their goal through excessive haste; grasping a pearl, they throw it at a magpie [?], sometimes letting a small gain obstruct a great undertaking. These men certainly differ from those who are vainly arrogant and rely on mere mettle. Nevertheless, their strength can be bent, their impatience provoked, their pride exploited, and their desires indulged to keep them in thrall. If entrusted with managing the affairs of the world, they will produce a mixture of successes and failures; one cannot plan with them with confidence of success. These are men whose judgment cannot govern their talent.
A grade above them are those who maintain strict boundaries between the inner self and the outer world and carefully judge how to act and respond. text:

與斷也將謂天下之事非已莫能成耳其
晰微制決持危定傾能於轉盼咄嗟之間
而竪俶儻不羣之績此四人者之能事也
然而其光外朗其氣內盈尋之不易其方
而測之可窮其際是無得乎養而未盛者

用其明勇蓋萬夫而不自任其力隨事而

translation_en:
…suppose that no one but himself can discern the workings of the world. Judging his own courage sufficient to make decisions, he will suppose that no one but himself can accomplish the world's affairs. Discerning subtleties and making decisions, sustaining what is endangered and steadying what is tottering, he can establish extraordinary and unequalled achievements in the blink of an eye or the space of an utterance. Such are the capabilities of these four men. Yet their brilliance shines outward, and their vital energy fills them inwardly. When one traces their course, they do not readily change direction; when one measures them, their limits can be reached. These are men who have gained nothing from cultivation and have not yet attained fullness [?]. Their rank is superior.

One grade higher are those whose wisdom comprehends the myriad things, yet who do not rely exclusively on their own discernment; whose courage surpasses that of ten thousand men, yet who do not rely exclusively on their own strength. They respond as circumstances arise, without clinging to preconceived judgments; they act in accordance with principle, without being drawn by achievement or profit. Before the first signs have emerged or discernible patterns have appeared, they deliberate alone in profound stillness, and the common people see no trace of their activity. Achievements unmatched in an age and benefits lasting for all ages are suddenly established on a grand scale, yet the common people do not know how this has come about. None of those whom the world calls wise or courageous can hope to match them. These are what Master Zhu called true heroes and outstanding men who are also sages and worthies. Theirs is the highest rank. I have attempted to survey the deeds of past and present on this basis and to assess comprehensively the capacities of historical figures. The distinctions of superiority and inferiority, of higher and lower standing, among heroes and outstanding men generally fall within these four categories. Yet even if the attendants were changed, they could not readily all be enumerated.

text:

子號為四豪漢高坐屈羣策以建纂堯之
業則張良蕭何韓信三臣者皆人傑也而
漢之得天下由是焉昭烈知人待士以噓
炎劉之燼則諸葛亮董允蔣琬費禕四子
者皆英雋也而蜀之存亡因之焉即史傳
所記固各有英雄豪傑之目矣試執前四

所記固各有英雄豪傑之目矣試執前四
者之等以槩此數子之長則七雄者彼哉
無以議爲也平原畢畢不及格矣孟嘗春
===
申廣交養名背公死黨奸人之魁耳信陵
威信於殭秦義存乎弱趙急人之難不屠
乎功盖猶有烈士之風焉惟其挾威震主
內疑外忌則君子所不道者其在三四之
間乎三傑遭際興運各奮才智推戴漢祖
卒成帝業信乎爲代寶矣子房英略盖世
而貌若處子功成身退超然遠引比之何
信爲最優焉三品之上者乎董允蔣琬費
禕端謹節士耳雖事無過舉然天之所授
punctuated: 國之末，貴臣握柄，資贍游談，於是列國公子號為四豪。漢高坐屈羣策，以建纂堯之業，則張良、蕭何、韓信三臣者皆人傑也，而漢之得天下由是焉。昭烈知人待士，以噓炎劉之燼，則諸葛亮、董允、蔣琬、費禕四子者皆英雋也，而蜀之存亡因之焉。即史傳所記，固各有英雄豪傑之目矣。試執前四者之等，以槩此數子之長，則七雄者，彼哉，無以議為也！平原卑卑，不及格矣。孟嘗、春申廣交養名，背公死黨，奸人之魁耳。信陵威信於疆秦，義存乎弱趙，急人之難，不居乎功，盖猶有烈士之風焉。惟其挟威震主，內疑外忌，則君子所不道者，其在三四之間乎？三傑遭際興運，各奮才智，推戴漢祖，卒成帝業，信乎為國寶矣！子房英略盖世，而貌若處子，功成身退，超然遠引，比之何、信為最優焉。三品之上者乎？董允、蔣琬、費禕，端謹節士耳。雖事無過舉，然天之所授
translation_en:
…at the end of the Warring States period, powerful ministers held the reins of government and provided financial support to itinerant persuaders. Thus the noble sons of the various states came to be known as the Four Magnates. Gaozu of Han brought the counsels of his many advisers into his service [?], thereby establishing a dynasty that continued Yao’s legacy. His three ministers, Zhang Liang, Xiao He, and Han Xin, were all outstanding men, and through them Han gained the empire. Emperor Zhaolie recognized men’s abilities and treated worthy men with consideration, breathing life into the embers of the Liu house of Han, associated with the virtue of Fire. Zhuge Liang, Dong Yun, Jiang Wan, and Fei Yi were all men of exceptional talent, and Shu’s survival or destruction depended upon them. In the historical accounts, then, each was accorded some designation as a hero or outstanding man.

Let us apply the four grades set out above to assess these men’s strengths. As for the Seven Powers, such men are beneath discussion! The Lord of Pingyuan was mediocre and fell short of the standard. The Lords of Mengchang and Chunshen cultivated extensive connections and fostered their reputations, turning their backs on the public good and devoting themselves to their factions even unto death. They were merely the foremost among unscrupulous men. The Lord of Xinling made his might felt in powerful Qin and, through righteous action, preserved weak Zhao. He hastened to relieve others’ distress and claimed no credit for his achievements: he retained something of the spirit of a man of high resolve. Yet he wielded power that intimidated his ruler, arousing suspicion within and apprehension abroad—conduct a gentleman would not commend. Would he perhaps rank between the third and fourth grades?

The Three Outstanding Men encountered the rising fortunes of a new dynasty. Each exerted his talents and wisdom in support of Gaozu of Han, ultimately establishing his imperial achievement. Truly, they were treasures of the state! Zifang [Zhang Liang] possessed heroic strategic ability surpassing his age, yet his appearance was that of a maiden. Once his work was accomplished, he withdrew from office, rising above worldly concerns and retiring far away. Compared with Xiao He and Han Xin, he was the best. Might he stand at the top of the third grade?

Dong Yun, Jiang Wan, and Fei Yi were simply upright, conscientious men of integrity. Although they committed no errors in conducting affairs, what Heaven had bestowed upon them…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
非特異也有忝英稱矣孔明望重於卧龍
力抗乎漢鼎君臣契合投袂匡時至於出
師獻納之言寧靜澹泊之語出處議論庶
幾王者之佐焉盖入其域而未優者乎之
數子者皆以盖世之才際功名之會雲蒸
龍變鷹揚虎視考其平生之所建植可謂
俊偉卓犖矣然其中或得分有多寡賦才
有無偏細節多疎則不能無負俗之累氣
質偏勝則不能無瑕纇之存盖所謂衆材
===
之尤也非衆尤之尤也必也其大禹乎鑿
龍門排伊闕别九州宅四隩績固偉矣然
且不矜不伐而莫與爭功愚夫愚婦而凛
若勝予彼視地平天成於吾身何有輕重
也其周公乎除兇殘驅虎豹立綱紀陳禮
樂功莫大焉然且吐哺握髮下白屋之士
不驕不吝履赤舄之安彼視勝殷遏劉於
吾心何有加損也其孔子乎學殫累世而
不以智聞力抉門關而不以勇聞在鄉黨

有兼偏細節多疎則不能無負俗之累氣
質偏勝則不能無瑕纇之存蓋所謂衆材
===

吾心何有加損也其孔子乎學殫累世而
不以智聞力扶門關而不以勇聞在鄉黨
punctuated:
非特異也，有忝英稱矣。孔明望重於卧龍，力抗乎漢鼎，君臣契合，投袂匡時。至於出師獻納之言，寧靜澹泊之語，出處議論，庶幾王者之佐焉。盖入其域而未優者乎？之數子者，皆以盖世之才，際功名之會，雲蒸龍變，鷹揚虎視。考其平生之所建植，可謂俊偉卓犖矣。然其中或得分有多寡，賦才有無偏，細節多疎，則不能無負俗之累；氣質偏勝，則不能無瑕纇之存。盖所謂衆材之尤也，非衆尤之尤也。
必也其大禹乎？鑿龍門，排伊闕，别九州，宅四隩，績固偉矣。然且不矜不伐，而莫與爭功；愚夫愚婦，而凛若勝予。彼視地平天成，於吾身何有輕重也？其周公乎？除兇殘，驅虎豹，立綱紀，陳禮樂，功莫大焉。然且吐哺握髮，下白屋之士；不驕不吝，履赤舄之安。彼視勝殷遏劉，於吾心何有加損也？其孔子乎？學殫累世，而不以智聞；力抉門關，而不以勇聞；在鄉黨
translation_en:
…were not exceptionally endowed, and thus fell short of the designation “outstanding.” Kongming’s reputation was exalted as the Sleeping Dragon; with all his strength he upheld the Han dynasty. Ruler and minister were of one mind, and he sprang into action to set his age aright. As for the counsel he offered when setting forth on campaign, and his words on tranquility and freedom from worldly desires, his conduct in office and retirement and his pronouncements approached those of an assistant to a true king. Had he perhaps entered that realm without yet attaining excellence within it? These several men [?], all possessing talents surpassing their age, encountered opportunities for achievement and fame. Like gathering clouds and transforming dragons, soaring hawks and watchful tigers, they rose to prominence. Examining what they established throughout their lives, one may indeed call them remarkable and outstanding. Yet among them, some received greater or lesser shares of natural endowment, and their talents were either balanced or partial [?]. Negligence in minor matters inevitably burdened them with the reproach of prevailing opinion; an excessive predominance of one aspect of their temperament inevitably left flaws. They were, as the saying goes, the outstanding among the many talented, rather than the most outstanding among the outstanding.
Surely it must be Da Yu? He cut through Longmen, opened a passage at Yique, distinguished the Nine Provinces, and made the four farthest regions habitable. His achievements were certainly magnificent. Yet he neither presumed upon them nor boasted, and none could rival his accomplishments. Before even ignorant men and women, he remained reverently apprehensive, as though they surpassed him. In his eyes, what weight could bringing order to the earth and completing Heaven’s work add to his own person? Or was it the Duke of Zhou? He eliminated the vicious and cruel, drove away tigers and leopards, established the governing principles of order, and instituted rites and music. No achievement was greater. Yet he spat out his food and held his unbound hair to receive visitors, humbling himself before scholars from plain dwellings. Neither arrogant nor miserly, he wore the red ceremonial shoes of high office with ease. In his eyes, what could conquering Yin and ending slaughter add to or subtract from his own heart? Or was it Kongzi? His learning encompassed the accumulated knowledge of generations, yet he was not renowned for cleverness; his strength could wrench up a gate bar, yet he was not renowned for valor. In his native community…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
而恂恂居朝廷而唯唯謹固儼然儒者也及
其却萊兵反鄆讙堕三都誅正卯即慷慨
竒節之士决眥奮臂極力而不能辦者乃
不動聲色徐引而振之既振油然而退無
矜容無盛氣此豈世之君子所可與量尺
寸哉盖此三聖人者受之於天既皆得夫
渾淪磅礴之氣修之於己又皆懋夫沉潛
純粹之學其所基者宥而密而所蓄者完
而固也故能决大疑排大難建大功立大
===
節紓徐委蛇而不見其作為之迹嗟夫非
天下之至聖其孰能與於此哉故朱子謂
真正英雄皆自戰兢中來而聖賢豪傑唯
此三聖人足以當之信不誣矣然則世之
君子受天地特厚之才而有志於三聖人
之事者顧可不慎所養乎養之之道無欲
其本也慎動其要也析義窮理沉幾察微
瑩乎若夜光之內朗洞乎若止水之獨鑑
所以養智也抑其彊陽銷其客氣深乎若

而恂恂居朝廷而唯唯謹固儼然儒者也及
其却莱兵反鄆讙龜陰墮三都誅正卯即慷慨
奇節之士決皆奮臂扼腕力而不能辦者乃
不動聲色徐引而振振之既振油然而退無
矜容無盛氣此豈世之君子所可與量尺
寸哉蓋此三聖人者受之於天既皆得夫
渾淪磅礴之氣修之於己又皆懋夫沉潛
純粹之學其所基者宥而密而所蓄者完
而固也故能決大疑排大難建大功立大
===
節紓徐委蛇而不見其作爲之迹嗟夫衆
天下之至聖其孰能與於此哉故朱子謂
真正英雄皆自戰兢中來而聖賢豪傑唯
此三聖人足以當之信不誣矣然則世之
君子受天地特厚之才而有志於三聖人
之事者顧可不慎所養乎養之之道無欲
其本也慎動其要也析義窮理沉幾察微
瑩乎若夜光之内朗洞乎若止水之獨鑑
所以養智也抑其殭陽銷其客氣深乎若
punctuated:
而恂恂，居朝廷而唯唯，謹固儼然儒者也。及其却萊兵、反鄆讙、堕三都、誅正卯，即慷慨竒節之士决眥奮臂、極力而不能辦者，乃不動聲色，徐引而振之。既振，油然而退，無矜容，無盛氣。此豈世之君子所可與量尺寸哉！盖此三聖人者，受之於天，既皆得夫渾淪磅礴之氣；修之於己，又皆懋夫沉潛純粹之學。其所基者宥而密，而所蓄者完而固也。故能决大疑、排大難、建大功、立大節，紓徐委蛇，而不見其作為之迹。嗟夫！非天下之至聖，其孰能與於此哉！故朱子謂真正英雄皆自戰兢中來，而聖賢豪傑唯此三聖人足以當之，信不誣矣。

然則世之君子，受天地特厚之才，而有志於三聖人之事者，顧可不慎所養乎？養之之道，無欲其本也，慎動其要也。析義窮理，沉幾察微，瑩乎若夜光之內朗，洞乎若止水之獨鑑，所以養智也。抑其彊陽，銷其客氣，深乎若
translation_en:
…he was mild and deferential, and at court he responded with respectful assent: cautious, steadfast, and dignified, he was a true Confucian scholar. Yet when he repelled the troops of Lai, recovered Yun and Huan, demolished the fortifications of the three cities, and executed Zhengmao, he accomplished what even men of ardent spirit and extraordinary integrity could not achieve, though they strained their eyes, raised their arms, and exerted all their strength. Without changing his voice or expression, he calmly took matters in hand and set them right. Once this was done, he withdrew at ease, showing neither pride nor overbearing spirit. How could the gentlemen of the world measure themselves against him!

These three sages, in what they received from Heaven, all possessed its undivided and boundless vital force; in cultivating themselves, they all diligently pursued profound and pure learning. The foundations they laid were broad and closely knit, and what they stored within was complete and firm. Thus they could resolve great uncertainties, overcome great difficulties, establish great achievements, and uphold great moral principles, all with such ease and composure that no trace of their exertion could be seen. Alas! Who but the supreme sages of the world could attain this? Thus Master Zhu said that true heroes all emerge from vigilance and trembling caution. Among sages, worthies, and outstanding men, only these three sages fully deserve that designation: this is indeed no false claim.

Then can the gentlemen of the world, endowed by Heaven and Earth with exceptionally abundant talents and aspiring to the deeds of these three sages, fail to take care over what they cultivate within themselves? In the way of such cultivation, freedom from desire is the foundation, and caution in action is the essential point. To distinguish what is right and investigate principles to their utmost, to ponder the incipient stirrings of things and discern the subtle, to be lustrous like the inward radiance of a night-shining pearl and clear like still water reflecting alone—these are the means of cultivating wisdom. To restrain one's forceful impetuosity, to dissolve one's transient passions, to be profound like…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
彊弩之握機韜乎若寶劔之斂鍔所以養
勇也尸居而龍見雷聲而淵黙聖人之事
也即史冊所載瑰偉奇特之士猶將姑舍
是焉而況其下者乎蓋嘗聞紀渻子之養
闘雞也始也虛憍而恃氣馴之十日則應
景響矣又十日然後其德全而異雞無敢
闘者矣此養德之喻也故英雄豪傑之從
事於學也若紀渻子之養雞也則幾矣
第四問
===
同考試官署郎中王 批〔真才為用久任責實皆官人急務此作𠻳激詳悉識見𧇊綽〕
同考試官右給事中顧 批〔畫八策於條擬詳盡且詞氣𠗂整有建白体塠武後風〕
同考試官檢討陳 批〔聖王鼓舞才賢獨在賞罰是作詳官人條法歷歷明悉末復歸重于此允為確論〕
同考試官編修何 批〔條論人材犁然允當而四議一納鑿鑿可行是必留心人物者〕
banxin: 會試錄文 六十一 夏洪憲
alt_text:
彊弩之握機韜乎若寳劒之斂鍔所以養
勇也尸居而龍見雷聲而淵默聖人之事
也即史冊所載瓌偉奇特之士猶將姑舍
是焉而况其下者乎蓋嘗聞紀渻子之養
鬭雞也始也虛憍而恃氣驟之十日則應
影嚮矣又十日然後其德全而異雞無敢
鬭者矣此養德之喻也故英雄豪傑之從
事於學也蓋紀渻子之養雞也則幾矣
第四問
===
同考試官署郎中王　批〔議論□□□文佳□□實　官人〕
同考試官右給事中□　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□詞氣〕
〔□□□□□□□□〕
同考試官檢討陳　批〔□□三□□才實獨在□罰□□〕
〔作牌官人條法歷歷明悉末復歸重于此允為確論〕
同考試官編修何　批〔條論人材犂然允當而□識〕
〔□□□可行是必留心人物者〕
punctuated:
彊弩之握機，韜乎若寶劔之斂鍔，所以養勇也。尸居而龍見，雷聲而淵黙，聖人之事也。即史冊所載瑰偉奇特之士，猶將姑舍是焉，而況其下者乎？蓋嘗聞紀渻子之養闘雞也：始也虛憍而恃氣，馴之十日，則應景響矣；又十日，然後其德全，而異雞無敢闘者矣。此養德之喻也。故英雄豪傑之從事於學也，若紀渻子之養雞也，則幾矣。

第四問

同考試官署郎中王批〔真才為用，久任責實，皆官人急務。此作𠻳激詳悉，識見𧇊綽。〕

同考試官右給事中顧批〔畫八策於條擬，詳盡，且詞氣𠗂整，有建白体，塠武後風。〕

同考試官檢討陳批〔聖王鼓舞才賢，獨在賞罰。是作詳官人條法，歷歷明悉，末復歸重于此，允為確論。〕

同考試官編修何批〔條論人材，犁然允當，而四議一納，鑿鑿可行，是必留心人物者。〕
translation_en:
…a powerful crossbow with its trigger held in check, concealed like a precious sword with its edge sheathed: this is how courage is cultivated. To remain still like a ritual personator of the dead yet manifest oneself like a dragon, to resound like thunder yet remain silent as a deep pool—these are the deeds of a sage. Even the extraordinary and remarkable men recorded in the histories must for the moment be set aside in this regard; how much more so those beneath them? I have heard of Ji Shengzi’s training of a fighting cock. At first it was vainly arrogant and relied on its aggressive spirit. After ten days of training, it still responded to shadows and sounds. After another ten days, its powers were fully developed, and no other cock dared fight it. This is an analogy for cultivating virtue. Thus, if heroes and outstanding men pursue learning as Ji Shengzi trained his cock, they will come close to the ideal.

Fourth Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Acting Bureau Director: “Employing genuine talent, retaining officials in office for long terms, and demanding substantive results are all urgent tasks in appointing officials. This composition is forceful [?] and thorough, and its discernment is ample [?].”

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Right Supervising Secretary: “It sets out eight measures in itemized proposals, treating them exhaustively. Its language and tone are orderly [?], and it has the form of a submission of recommendations, following in the footsteps of earlier models [?].”

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Examining Editor: “The sage king’s means of inspiring the talented and worthy lie solely in rewards and punishments. This composition explains in detail the rules and procedures for appointing officials, presenting each clearly and fully. At the end it again places the chief emphasis on this point. It is indeed a sound argument.”

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Compiling Editor: “Its itemized discussion of human talent is clear and fitting, and its ‘four proposals and one acceptance’ [?] are demonstrably practicable. The author must be someone who pays close attention to people and their qualities.”

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
考試官學士呂批辨論官材之法講究詳明且以賞
罰二柄責之用人者最為有見取之
考試官大學士張批鑒別品流極為精當官人之法盡
於此矣錄之
夫臧否人物以信萬世儒者之論也甄叙
羣材以易海內聖王之術也儒者挾冊而
談古昔品藻當世覩淑慝之歸而立取舍
之極其事貴核而其論貴定何者信萬世

translation_en:
Examiner Lü, Academician, comments: The methods for assessing talent for office are examined thoroughly and clearly. Moreover, the essay holds those who employ men responsible for wielding the two powers of reward and punishment. This is especially perceptive. Accept it.

Examiner Zhang, Grand Secretary, comments: Its distinctions among the various grades of men are exceptionally precise and apt. The methods of appointing men to office are fully covered here. Select it.

To judge the merits and faults of men so that those judgments command trust for ten thousand generations is the province of Confucian scholars’ discourse; to select and rank the many talents so as to transform all within the seas is the art of the sage kings. Confucian scholars, books in hand, discuss antiquity and appraise their contemporaries. Observing where goodness and wickedness lead, they establish the ultimate standards for acceptance and rejection. Their investigations must be exact, and their judgments firm. Why? Because they must command trust for ten thousand generations.

How much more is this true of a ruler who employs the talents of the realm to undertake its affairs, weighs and distinguishes the various grades of men, and ranks officials from worst to best in order to punish and reward them! A single mistaken judgment of merit or fault confounds the worthy with the unworthy; a single ill-measured censure or promotion confuses men about what to pursue and what to avoid. Yet ruler and ministers are separated by the distinction between the hall and its steps; men’s dispositions are more treacherous than mountains and rivers; discernment is obscured by things as minute as a hair or eyelash; and what the ruler hears is confused by the monthly appraisals of men. Is it not difficult to know all the talents of the realm and employ them to the fullest?

The sage king assesses men as though using scales and measures: he weighs and measures each one, down to the smallest units, without error. Thus he appoints men only after settling his assessments, assigns duties according to ability, wholeheartedly entrusts them with affairs, examines their actual performance, and evaluates their overall accomplishments. Only then does each appointment suit the man’s talents, and each man’s talents find their fullest use. All undertakings flourish, and orderly government throughout the realm is achieved. The Book of Documents says: “To know men is to be discerning …”

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
能官人可不慎歟是故折衷儒者之論而
通于聖王之術則可以語知人也已愚嘗
讀班固古今人表其列九等之叙何其辨
也盖其說曰可與為善不可與為惡是謂
上智可與為惡不可與為善是謂下愚可
與為善可與為惡是謂中人故以聖人為
上上仁人為上中智人為上下愚人為下
下而其餘則皆中人謂其可導而上下也
此言才質之大較也然顔淵亞聖與管晏
===
並稱則諄矣伊傅大賢與叔向同列則舛
矣綴公伯寮祝鮀于老聃之後則非倫矣
揭曾參于游夏之末則失次矣其他踳駁
張晏盖嘗非之則是固之論人未當也又
嘗讀劉劭人物志其言十二流之業何其
詳也盖其說曰清節之德師氏之任也法
家之材司寇之任也術家之材三孤之任
也三材純備三公之任也三材而微冢宰
之任也臧否之材師氏之佐也智意之材

punctuated: 能官人，可不慎歟？是故折衷儒者之論，而通于聖王之術，則可以語知人也已。愚嘗讀班固《古今人表》，其列九等之叙，何其辨也！盖其說曰：「可與為善，不可與為惡，是謂上智；可與為惡，不可與為善，是謂下愚；可與為善，可與為惡，是謂中人。」故以聖人為上上，仁人為上中，智人為上下，愚人為下下，而其餘則皆中人，謂其可導而上下也。此言才質之大較也。然顔淵亞聖，與管晏並稱，則諄矣；伊傅大賢，與叔向同列，則舛矣；綴公伯寮、祝鮀于老聃之後，則非倫矣；揭曾參于游夏之末，則失次矣。其他踳駁，張晏盖嘗非之，則是固之論人未當也。又嘗讀劉劭《人物志》，其言十二流之業，何其詳也！盖其說曰：「清節之德，師氏之任也；法家之材，司寇之任也；術家之材，三孤之任也；三材純備，三公之任也；三材而微，冢宰之任也；臧否之材，師氏之佐也；智意之材
translation_en: …able to appoint people to office. Can one fail to exercise care? Thus, by weighing the judgments of Confucian scholars and comprehending the methods of the sage kings, one may indeed speak of knowing people. I have read Ban Gu’s Table of People Past and Present: how discriminating its arrangement into nine grades appears! His explanation runs: “Those with whom one can do good but cannot do evil are called supremely wise; those with whom one can do evil but cannot do good are called utterly foolish; those with whom one can do either good or evil are called middling people.” Accordingly, he places sages in the highest grade of the upper rank, benevolent people in its middle grade, wise people in its lowest grade, and fools in the lowest grade of the lower rank. All the remainder are middling people, meaning that they can be guided upward or downward. This describes the broad outlines of talent and disposition. Yet to rank Yan Yuan, who approached sagehood, alongside Guan Zhong and Yan Ying is confused [?]; to place the great worthies Yi Yin and Fu Yue in the same class as Shuxiang is mistaken; to append Gongbo Liao and Zhu Tuo after Lao Dan groups together people of unlike kind; and to put Zeng Shen after Ziyou and Zixia misorders their ranks. Zhang Yan has already criticized other inconsistencies in the table. Thus Ban Gu’s judgments of people were not sound. I have also read Liu Shao’s Treatise on Human Character: how detailed its account of the work appropriate to twelve types of people appears! His explanation runs: “The virtue of unsullied integrity qualifies one for the duties of a Mentor; talent in law qualifies one for the duties of Minister of Justice; talent in statecraft qualifies one for the duties of the Three Junior Preceptors. Complete and unalloyed possession of these three talents qualifies one for the duties of the Three Dukes; possession of the three in lesser measure qualifies one for the duties of Chief Minister. Talent in judging merit and fault qualifies one to assist the Mentor; talent in devising strategies…”

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
冢宰之佐也伎倆之材司空之任也儒學
之材安民之任也文章之材國史之任也
辯給之材行人之任也驍雄之材將帥之
任也是言任官之大法也然子產遺愛儕
于西門則精粗不辨矣樂毅傑材等于曹
丘則忠讒無別矣目趙張爲伎倆則能吏
之績隱矣名子夏之徒爲臧否則洙泗之
傳晦矣其諸疵類李德裕亦嘗非之則是
劭之論人未至也甚矣論人之難而知人
===
之不易也愚竊評之固之書繁瑣蕪蔓使
人眩瞀而不知其歸然其論材質之大較
則可采已劭之書闇于大道使人摘其疵
而議其非然其論任官之大法不可易已
君人者會通而推廣之則知人用人之道
豈外是哉今天下之需才甚于農之望歲
也
明天子拊髀而思側席而求公卿持籌而畫計
臣謀士扼腕而談非一日矣乃天下有急

則可采已劭之書闊于大道使人摘其疵

君人者會通而推廣之則知人用人之道

也
===
明天子拊髀而思側席而求公卿持籌而畫計
臣謀士扼腕而談非一日矣乃天下有急
punctuated:
冢宰之佐也；伎倆之材，司空之任也；儒學之材，安民之任也；文章之材，國史之任也；辯給之材，行人之任也；驍雄之材，將帥之任也。是言任官之大法也。然子產遺愛，儕于西門，則精粗不辨矣；樂毅傑材，等于曹丘，則忠讒無別矣；目趙張爲伎倆，則能吏之績隱矣；名子夏之徒爲臧否，則洙泗之傳晦矣。其諸疵類，李德裕亦嘗非之，則是劭之論人未至也。甚矣，論人之難，而知人之不易也！
愚竊評之：固之書繁瑣蕪蔓，使人眩瞀而不知其歸，然其論材質之大較，則可采已；劭之書闇于大道，使人摘其疵而議其非，然其論任官之大法，不可易已。君人者會通而推廣之，則知人用人之道，豈外是哉？今天下之需才，甚于農之望歲也。明天子拊髀而思，側席而求，公卿持籌而畫，計臣謀士扼腕而談，非一日矣。乃天下有急
translation_en:
…are suited to assisting the Chief Minister; those with technical abilities, to the duties of Minister of Works; those versed in Confucian learning, to bringing peace to the people; those with literary abilities, to the duties of State Historiographer; those with ready eloquence, to the duties of Messenger; and those of martial prowess, to commanding armies. These statements set out the fundamental principles of appointing officials. Yet placing Zichan, whose benevolent legacy endured, alongside Ximen fails to distinguish the refined from the coarse. Equating the outstanding talents of Yue Yi with those of Cao Qiu fails to distinguish loyalty from slander. Classifying Zhao and Zhang as men of technical abilities obscures their achievements as capable officials. Describing Zixia and his followers as men skilled in appraising merits and faults obscures the transmission of Confucius’s teachings from the Zhu and Si rivers. Li Deyu also criticized such defects. Thus Shao’s judgments of men were not fully adequate. How very difficult it is to judge men, and how far from easy to know them!
I venture, in my ignorance, to offer this assessment: Gu’s book is excessively detailed and overgrown with material, leaving readers bewildered and unable to discern its drift. Yet its broad account of talents and dispositions is worth adopting. Shao’s book lacks understanding of the Great Way, inviting readers to pick out its defects and criticize its errors. Yet its fundamental principles for appointing officials cannot be altered. If a ruler integrates their insights and extends their application, could the way of knowing and employing men lie beyond these? Today the realm’s need for talent is more urgent than a farmer’s longing for a good harvest. Our enlightened Son of Heaven slaps his thigh in thought and sits sideways on his seat in eager search for worthy men; dukes and ministers deliberate with counting rods in hand, while fiscal officials and advisers clasp their wrists in impassioned discussion. This has gone on for more than a day. Yet when an emergency arises in the realm…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
率稱乏材何也夫十步之內必有豐草今
以宇內之廣環四海之外爲帶而謂無才
可乎然而人之負材也異弗可弗辨也夫
天下有全材亦有偏材有真材亦有似材
并包眾能囊括百行謨謀足以制廟勝設
施足以裨王畧指顧而疆圉寧談咲而社
稷安靡發不當靡施不効如是者全材也
長于辨一官而短于爲一國明于見一方
而闇于制萬里守文則工應變則拙任劇
===
務則理持大柄則疎如是者偏材也質純
以慤行直以方量弘以深氣剛以塞不衒
𥨸以爲功不矜飾以釣名如是者真材也
狡獪儇詞以爲智突梯脂韋以爲通矯飾
矜名以爲廉譏時好訕以爲直謾談陳說
以爲辨恣睢暴戾以爲強言不顧行實不
中聲如是者似材也然全材難能而偏材
者恒易失真材難得而似材者恒易眩在
慎所用而已今夫楩枏杞梓皆材也纖者

以宇内之廣環四海之外爲帶而謂無才

率稱乏材，何也？夫十步之內，必有豐草。今以宇內之廣，環四海之外爲帶，而謂無才，可乎？然而人之負材也異，弗可弗辨也。夫天下有全材，亦有偏材；有真材，亦有似材。并包眾能，囊括百行，謨謀足以制廟勝，設施足以裨王畧，指顧而疆圉寧，談咲而社稷安，靡發不當，靡施不効，如是者全材也。長于辨一官而短于爲一國，明于見一方而闇于制萬里，守文則工，應變則拙，任劇務則理，持大柄則疎，如是者偏材也。質純以慤，行直以方，量弘以深，氣剛以塞，不衒𥨸以爲功，不矜飾以釣名，如是者真材也。狡獪儇詞以爲智，突梯脂韋以爲通，矯飾矜名以爲廉，譏時好訕以爲直，謾談陳說以爲辨，恣睢暴戾以爲強，言不顧行，實不中聲，如是者似材也。然全材難能，而偏材者恒易失；真材難得，而似材者恒易眩。在慎所用而已。
今夫楩枏杞梓，皆材也，纖者
translation_en:
…they invariably claim that men of talent are lacking. Why is this? Within ten paces there must be luxuriant grass. Given the vastness of the realm, encircled by a girdle beyond the Four Seas, can one say that there is no talent? Yet people differ in the talents they possess, and these differences must be discerned. There are men of comprehensive talent and men of specialized talent; there are men of genuine talent and men whose talent is only apparent. Those who embrace many abilities and encompass every virtuous practice, whose deliberations suffice to secure victory through planning in the ancestral temple and whose measures further royal strategy, who bring peace to the frontiers with a gesture and secure the altars of soil and grain amid conversation and laughter, whose every initiative is appropriate and every undertaking effective—these are men of comprehensive talent. Those adept at managing one office but deficient in governing a state, perceptive about one region but unable to administer a territory of ten thousand li, skillful in observing established rules but clumsy in responding to change, orderly in handling demanding affairs but careless when wielding supreme authority—these are men of specialized talent. Those whose nature is pure and sincere, whose conduct is upright and principled, whose capacity is broad and deep, whose vital spirit is firm and full, who do not parade stolen accomplishments as their own merit [?] or seek renown through boastful embellishment—these are men of genuine talent. Those who pass off cunning and glib speech as wisdom, slippery pliancy as practical understanding, affected conduct and concern for reputation as incorruptibility, criticism of the times and a fondness for slander as frankness, empty talk and rehearsed assertions as eloquence, and unbridled violence as strength, whose words take no account of their deeds and whose substance does not match their reputation—these are men whose talent is only apparent. Yet comprehensive talent is difficult to attain, while men of specialized talent are constantly liable to be overlooked; genuine talent is difficult to find, while men of apparent talent readily dazzle others. It is simply a matter of taking care whom one employs.

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
不可使鉅而挺者不能為屈然匠氏操引
而施斲焉則各致其用以相成也物固有
似是而實非者魚目雜珠燕石亂玉鮮不
易視矣腊鼠混璞車軜疑朔鮮不易聽矣
而有識者常謹辨之夫用才亦若是也偏
者不以全棄真者不以似眩然後可以致
材用而責成功是故廣登籲之途明器使
之道公久任之法核功效之實此四者議
之所急也何以明之夫世無粹白之狐而
===
有粹白之裘者所求博也今才所繇進直
三途耳然貢于學官者以遲暮見摧起于
掾史者以刀筆見廢其所以肩鴻鉅而濟
緩急者則取諸佔畢文詞之薄技耳彼巖
穴之夫冗散之吏即有跅弛揮霍之才蔑
由進也故登籲之途宜廣也語有之騏驥
不可以逐鼠殊性也梁麗不可以窒穴殊

而有識者常謹辨之夫用才亦若是也論

用也今率以一人更數職通河渠者復責
以法律習錢穀者復責以甲兵是古稷卨
punctuated:
不可使鉅，而挺者不能為屈。然匠氏操引而施斲焉，則各致其用以相成也。物固有似是而實非者：魚目雜珠，燕石亂玉，鮮不易視矣；腊鼠混璞，車軜疑朔，鮮不易聽矣。而有識者常謹辨之。夫用才亦若是也：偏者不以全棄，真者不以似眩，然後可以致材用而責成功。是故廣登籲之途，明器使之道，公久任之法，核功效之實，此四者議之所急也。何以明之？夫世無粹白之狐，而有粹白之裘者，所求博也。今才所繇進，直三途耳。然貢于學官者以遲暮見摧，起于掾史者以刀筆見廢，其所以肩鴻鉅而濟緩急者，則取諸佔畢文詞之薄技耳。彼巖穴之夫、冗散之吏，即有跅弛揮霍之才，蔑由進也。故登籲之途宜廣也。
語有之：「騏驥不可以逐鼠，殊性也；梁麗不可以窒穴，殊用也。」今率以一人更數職，通河渠者復責以法律，習錢穀者復責以甲兵，是古稷卨
translation_en:
…cannot be made massive, and straight timber cannot be made to bend. Yet when a craftsman handles and hews it, each piece can serve its purpose and complement the others. There are certainly things that appear genuine but are not: fish eyes mingle with pearls, and stones from Yan pass for jade, seldom failing to deceive the eye; “dried rat” is confused with “uncut jade,” and “chariot reins” with “new moon” [?], seldom failing to deceive the ear. Discerning people, however, always distinguish them carefully. Employing talent is much the same: those whose abilities are limited should not be rejected for lacking comprehensive ability, and genuine talent should not be obscured by its counterfeit. Only then can talent be put to use and successful results demanded. Thus, broadening the avenues of recruitment, clarifying how to employ people according to their abilities, making the rules for long tenure impartial, and verifying actual achievements are the four matters most urgently requiring discussion. How can this be demonstrated? There are no wholly white foxes in the world, yet there are wholly white fox-fur robes, because the material is sought widely. Today there are only three avenues through which talented men can advance. Yet those recommended through the educational officials are held back because they are advanced in years, while those who rise from clerical service are rejected because of their association with the clerical brush and knife. Consequently, the men chosen to shoulder great responsibilities and meet emergencies are selected solely for the modest skills of textual study and literary composition. Recluses dwelling among cliffs and caves, and officials in idle or unimportant posts, have no avenue of advancement, even if they possess bold and unfettered talents. Thus the avenues of recruitment ought to be broadened.
There is a saying: “A thoroughbred cannot be used to chase mice: its nature is different. A great roof beam cannot be used to plug a hole: its use is different.” Today, however, a single man is routinely made to serve successively in several offices. One versed in rivers and canals is then charged with administering the law; one familiar with revenue and grain is then charged with military affairs. This is something that even Ji and Xie of antiquity …

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
夔龍之所不能兼唐虞之所不能彊也而
以責中世之士一試不效曹起而議之即
有他長不足贖矣故器使之道宜明也古
者為吏長子孫居官為姓氏無內外尊卑
一也今久任之法人人言之然卿寺藩臬
所謂尊官大吏者或歲遷月移席不暇暖
而以責疆埸之臣郡邑之吏夫孰不懷覬
覦之私而跂循資之擢乎令格于上而欲
法行于下不可得也故久任之法宜公也
===
蓋聞課織者縷而積之則無廢也吹竽者
一一而聽之則無濫也今愛憎殊途刺舉
異意薦墨未乾旋以垢聲斥矣謗書猶騰
遽以善狀聞矣獵名者以善飾售欺任質
者以著瑕蒙詬夫衡石之書一夫之頰不
可以為據也故功效之實宜核也今誠能
設辟舉之令開功名之門有跧伏林藪以
才薦焉則拔之有沉淪瑣列以才薦焉則
拔之無限科條無局常調則羣材畢出而

===
盖聞課織者縷而積之則無廢也吹竽者
一一而聽之則無濫也今釐憎殊途剌舉
異意薦墨未乾旋以垢聲斥矣謗書猶騰
遽以善狀聞矣獵名者以善飾售欺任質
者以著瑕蒙詬夫衡石之書一夫之類不
可以爲據也故功效之實宜核也今誠能

才薦焉則拔之有沉淪瑣列以才薦焉則
拔之無限科條無局常調則羣材畢出而
punctuated:
夔龍之所不能兼，唐虞之所不能彊也，而以責中世之士。一試不效，曹起而議之，即有他長，不足贖矣。故器使之道宜明也。古者為吏長，子孫居官，為姓氏，無內外尊卑，一也。今久任之法，人人言之，然卿寺藩臬，所謂尊官大吏者，或歲遷月移，席不暇暖，而以責疆埸之臣、郡邑之吏。夫孰不懷覬覦之私，而跂循資之擢乎？令格于上，而欲法行于下，不可得也。故久任之法宜公也。

蓋聞課織者，縷而積之，則無廢也；吹竽者，一一而聽之，則無濫也。今愛憎殊途，刺舉異意，薦墨未乾，旋以垢聲斥矣；謗書猶騰，遽以善狀聞矣。獵名者以善飾售欺，任質者以著瑕蒙詬。夫衡石之書、一夫之頰，不可以為據也。故功效之實宜核也。今誠能設辟舉之令，開功名之門，有跧伏林藪以才薦焉，則拔之；有沉淪瑣列以才薦焉，則拔之。無限科條，無局常調，則羣材畢出而
translation_en:
…even Kui and Long could not have combined these responsibilities, nor could the rulers of Tang and Yu have compelled them to do so. Yet such demands are imposed upon the men of later ages. If a single trial proves unsuccessful, critics rise together against them; whatever other strengths they possess cannot redeem them. Thus the principle of employing men according to their abilities must be made clear. In antiquity, when men served as officials and leaders, their descendants continued in office and took their offices as clan names [?]; the same practice applied to all, whether serving at court or outside it, in high or low positions. Today everyone speaks of the rule of long tenure. Yet the chief ministers and court officials, the provincial administration commissioners and surveillance commissioners—those whom we call high officials and great officers—may be transferred yearly or monthly, scarcely having time to warm their seats. Long tenure is nevertheless demanded of officials on the frontiers and those serving in prefectures and counties. Who among them would not harbor private ambitions and eagerly await promotion by seniority? When an ordinance is obstructed above, it is impossible to expect the rule to operate below. Thus the rule of long tenure must be applied impartially.

I have heard that, when assessing weaving, accumulating the work thread by thread ensures that nothing is wasted; when assessing players of the yu mouth organ, listening to them one by one ensures that no unqualified performer slips through. Today, affection and aversion lead in different directions, and impeachment and recommendation proceed from differing intentions. Before the ink on a recommendation has dried, the man is dismissed for an unsavory reputation; while defamatory reports are still circulating, a favorable account of his conduct is suddenly submitted. Those who hunt for fame pass off their deceptions through skillful embellishment, while those who rely on their unadorned character suffer abuse because their flaws are visible. Neither documents weighed out in great quantities nor a single man's tongue can be relied upon as evidence. Thus actual achievement must be verified. If we can now truly establish provisions for recruitment and recommendation and open the gates to achievement and distinction, then whenever someone living secluded in the forests is recommended for his abilities, let him be advanced; whenever someone languishing in a petty post is recommended for his abilities, let him be advanced. Impose no restrictions through formal regulations and no confinement within routine channels of appointment; then men of every talent will all come forward, and…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
應用不匱矣因材而授之事因事而試之
功取其一不責其二錄其所長不訾其所
短則功用相得而庶務畢張矣慎簡用重
遷擢位通顯者假以歲月而不撓其成積
功勞者優以職級而不易其處則人人以
誠處官而饕榮躁進者息矣以目正耳以
景察形治行有狀不搖于羣誹功善無聞
不惑于衆好無以一眚掩其大節無以一
事蓋其生平則事皆責實而陳功見偽者
===
阻矣由是偏材有所適于時而似材無所
害于治彼九等十二流者若數白黑而廢
置焉何患乎知人之難乎愚又聞之三軍
之衆一鼓皆作令所驅也一夫善射百人
决拾氣所激也故天下之士不叩不鳴不
觸不應古之聖王所以轉移世道鼓舞才
賢者操二柄以馭之而已施不測之賞以
待瓌偉卓犖之材用不測之罰以懲闒茸
嵬瑣之士則偏材者皆思累績鳩功以自

punctuated: 應用不匱矣。因材而授之事，因事而試之功，取其一，不責其二；錄其所長，不訾其所短，則功用相得而庶務畢張矣。慎簡用，重遷擢，位通顯者假以歲月而不撓其成，積功勞者優以職級而不易其處，則人人以誠處官而饕榮躁進者息矣。以目正耳，以景察形，治行有狀，不搖于羣誹；功善無聞，不惑于衆好。無以一眚掩其大節，無以一事蓋其生平，則事皆責實而陳功見偽者阻矣。由是偏材有所適于時，而似材無所害于治。彼九等十二流者，若數白黑而廢置焉，何患乎知人之難乎？愚又聞之：三軍之衆，一鼓皆作，令所驅也；一夫善射，百人决拾，氣所激也。故天下之士，不叩不鳴，不觸不應。古之聖王所以轉移世道、鼓舞才賢者，操二柄以馭之而已。施不測之賞以待瓌偉卓犖之材，用不測之罰以懲闒茸嵬瑣之士，則偏材者皆思累績鳩功以自
translation_en:
…and there will be no shortage of talent to meet practical needs. Assign men tasks according to their abilities, and assess their accomplishments according to those tasks. Accept a man's ability in one respect without demanding another; recognize his strengths without criticizing his shortcomings. Then achievement and employment will accord, and all public business will flourish. Be careful in selection and appointment, and deliberate in promotion. Allow those in prominent positions sufficient time, without disrupting their work before it bears fruit; favor those who have accumulated meritorious service with official rank, without changing their posts. Then everyone will serve sincerely in office, and those who hunger for glory and press impatiently for advancement will desist. Correct what the ears hear by what the eyes see; examine the form through its shadow. Where there is evidence of good administration, do not be swayed by widespread slander; where no meritorious deeds are known, do not be misled by general acclaim. Do not let a single fault obscure a man's greater integrity, or a single deed overshadow his whole life. Then actual results will be demanded in every undertaking, and those whose claims of achievement prove false will be checked.

Thus, men of specialized ability will find employment suited to the times, while men who merely appear talented will have no opportunity to harm government. As for those nine grades and twelve categories of men, dismissing or appointing them would be as straightforward as counting black and white objects. Why worry that knowing men is difficult? I have also heard this: when the hosts of the three armies all rise at one beat of the drum, it is commands that impel them; when one man excels at archery and a hundred men take up thumb rings and arm guards, it is ardor that stirs them. Thus, the scholars of the realm do not sound unless struck, nor respond unless stirred. The sage kings of antiquity transformed the ways of the world and roused talented and worthy men simply by wielding the two powers of reward and punishment to direct them. Bestow rewards beyond expectation upon men of magnificent and outstanding talent, and employ punishments beyond expectation to chastise base and petty men. Then those of specialized ability will all seek to accumulate achievements and amass merit so as to prove themselves…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
効而似材者亦洒心滌行事自濯磨是中
人者可上而一流二流者可企而三材也
尚何材用之不充理效之不著哉嗟夫庸
人之御馬也數策傷吻而不進使造父駕
齧𰯼驂乗旦則千里一息矣夫善用人者
之能致治其效亦若斯焉已
第五問
吳秀
同考試官都給事中韓批和以修守既見正畫而
末復以制虜之本望諸
朝廷尤折衝上策也錄之
===

translation_en:
…prove their worth, while those who merely appear talented will also cleanse their hearts and purify their conduct, striving to refine themselves. Thus people of middling ability can rise higher, and those of the first and second ranks can aspire to the three kinds of talent [?]. How, then, could talent remain insufficient for employment, or the results of good government fail to become manifest? Alas! When an ordinary man drives horses, he repeatedly whips them and injures their mouths, yet they do not advance. But let Zaofu drive Nie [?], with Chengdan as an outside horse, and they will cover a thousand li in a single breath. Those skilled in employing people can bring about good government with just such results.
Fifth Policy Question
Wu Xiu

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
今天下言邊事者豈不甚辨矣哉異日者
雲中上谷間歲歲苦虜
主上不得怡而謀臣武吏以為憂議戰議守如
救焚拯溺然今其勢則異矣虜歸我叛人
款關稱貢且乞封矣
朝廷宏覆載之仁帷幄得廟勝之策緣邊之
士父兄緩帶稚子咽哺有日矣廼執事猶
兢兢過厪內憂求所以隨時觀變計慮長
遠者嗟乎此人臣之極忠智士之苦思也
===
而愚何敢無說以對蓋聞治古之世自唐
虞首以夷狄猾夏為憂而當時君臣相告
勉稱率服者曰惇德允元焉頌來王者曰
克艱無怠焉既而舞兩階朝萬國格有苗
序西戎史書而記之聲施萬世而聖人不
以其故輟憂於叢挫忘警於幾康然則制
禦之術可知已及後世衰德不足以制夷
狄談說之士廼各以其意持籌畫計言人
人殊然大要無出戰守和三策而三者之
alt_text:
今天下言邊事者豈不甚難矣哉異日者
雲中上谷間歲歲苦虜
主上不得怡而謀臣武吏以爲憂議戰議守如
救焚拯溺然今其勢則異矣虜歸我叛人
款關稱貢且乞封矣
朝廷宏覆載之仁惟幄得廟勝之策緣邊之
士父兄緩帶稚子咽哺有日矣廼孰事猶
兢兢過慮内爱求所以隨時觀變計慮長
遠者嗟乎此人臣之極忠智士之苦思也
===
而愚何敢無說以對盖聞治古之世自唐
虞首以夷狄猾夏爲憂而當時君臣相告
勉稱率服者曰惇德允元焉續孝王者曰
克艱無怠焉既而舞兩階朝萬國格有苗
序西戎史書而記之聲施萬世而聖人不
以其故輟憂於叢挫忘警於幾康然則制
禦之術可知已及後世衰德不足以制夷
狄談說之士廼各以其意持籌畫計言人
人殊然大要無出戰守和三策而三者之
punctuated:
今天下言邊事者，豈不甚辨矣哉！異日者，雲中、上谷間，歲歲苦虜，主上不得怡，而謀臣武吏以為憂，議戰議守，如救焚拯溺然。今其勢則異矣：虜歸我叛人，款關稱貢，且乞封矣。朝廷宏覆載之仁，帷幄得廟勝之策，緣邊之士，父兄緩帶，稚子咽哺，有日矣。廼執事猶兢兢過厪內憂，求所以隨時觀變、計慮長遠者。嗟乎！此人臣之極忠、智士之苦思也。而愚何敢無說以對？

蓋聞治古之世，自唐虞首以夷狄猾夏為憂，而當時君臣相告勉，稱率服者曰「惇德允元」焉，頌來王者曰「克艱無怠」焉。既而舞兩階，朝萬國，格有苗，序西戎，史書而記之，聲施萬世，而聖人不以其故輟憂於叢挫、忘警於幾康。然則制禦之術可知已。及後世衰，德不足以制夷狄，談說之士廼各以其意持籌畫計，言人人殊。然大要無出戰、守、和三策，而三者之
translation_en:
Are not those throughout the realm who discuss frontier affairs today exceedingly eloquent! In former years, the regions of Yunzhong and Shanggu suffered annually from the enemy. His Majesty could find no peace, and his civil advisers and military officers were deeply concerned. They debated warfare and defense as urgently as if rescuing people from fire or drowning. Now, however, the situation has changed: the enemy has returned our renegades, approached the frontier gates offering tribute, and even requested investiture. The court has extended its benevolence, all-embracing like Heaven and Earth, and its military counselors have devised a strategy that secures victory through deliberations at court. For some time now, among the people along the frontier, fathers and elder brothers have been able to loosen their belts, and young children to eat their fill. Yet you, honored examiners, remain exceedingly vigilant and deeply concerned within, seeking ways to observe changes as circumstances evolve and to plan for the distant future. Ah! This is the utmost loyalty of a minister and the painstaking reflection of wise men. How, then, could I, ignorant though I am, dare offer no argument in reply?

I have heard that in the well-governed ages of antiquity, from the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, the disorder caused by the Yi and Di among the people of Xia was a foremost concern. The rulers and ministers of that time exhorted one another. In speaking of universal submission, they said, “Make virtue abundant and trust the good”; in celebrating those who came to acknowledge royal authority, they said, “Be equal to difficulties and never grow idle.” Thereupon, dances were performed between the two stairways, the myriad states came to court, the Youmiao were brought to submission, and the Western Rong were brought into order. Historians recorded these achievements, and their renown spread through all ages. Yet the sages did not on that account cease their concern amid accumulated setbacks [?], or forget vigilance when tranquility was near [?]. From this, the means of controlling and keeping the frontier peoples in check can be understood. When later ages declined, virtue no longer sufficed to control the Yi and Di. Men skilled in debate then devised strategies and plans according to their own views, each offering a different argument. Broadly speaking, however, these did not go beyond the three policies of warfare, defense, and peace; and among these three…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
中利害得失亦各異焉試以漢事籌之文
景襲婁敬之策發使約婚救安邊境民得
以緣南畝而海內用饒此和之效也然屈
中國以奉夷狄則辱矣孝武赫然命將封
狼胥禪姑衍匈奴逃北遠塞幕南無王庭
此戰之效也然罷士馬以勤遠略則黷矣
度河自朔方以西至今居築城通渠稍蠶
食北地而虜不敢爭此守之效也然轉漕
山東為費鉅萬戍卒未見省而閭左告病
===
則勞矣賈誼嘗憤匈奴之桀驁流涕漢庭
而其所謂三表五餌之策乃欲賜之盛服
車乘音樂婦人高堂邃宇倉庫奴婢又反
出於歲繒之下則疎矣厥後仲舒陳質子
之約安國止馬邑之師魏相陳無名之兵
蕭傅申恤禍之義言雖不同要其㫖歸則
班固所謂搢紳之儒專主和親耳愚嘗總
覽當時之事究觀諸臣之言大抵皆以敵
之彊弱為彊弱而非以已之彊弱為彊弱

而其所謂三表五餌之策乃欲賜之盛服

出於歲繒之下則疎矣厥後仲舒陳質子
之約安國止馬邑之師魏相陳無名之兵
蕭傅申恤禍之義言雖不同要其旨歸則
班固所謂縉紳之儒專主和親耳愚嘗總
覽當時之事究觀諸臣之言大抵皆以敵
之彊弱為彊弱而非以已之彊弱為彊弱
punctuated: 中，利害得失亦各異焉。試以漢事籌之：文景襲婁敬之策，發使約婚，救安邊境，民得以緣南畝，而海內用饒，此和之效也。然屈中國以奉夷狄，則辱矣。孝武赫然命將，封狼胥，禪姑衍，匈奴逃北遠塞，幕南無王庭，此戰之效也。然罷士馬以勤遠略，則黷矣。度河，自朔方以西至今居，築城通渠，稍蠶食北地，而虜不敢爭，此守之效也。然轉漕山東，為費鉅萬，戍卒未見省，而閭左告病，則勞矣。賈誼嘗憤匈奴之桀驁，流涕漢庭，而其所謂三表五餌之策，乃欲賜之盛服、車乘、音樂、婦人、高堂邃宇、倉庫、奴婢，又反出於歲繒之下，則疎矣。厥後，仲舒陳質子之約，安國止馬邑之師，魏相陳無名之兵，蕭傅申恤禍之義。言雖不同，要其㫖歸，則班固所謂搢紳之儒專主和親耳。愚嘗總覽當時之事，究觀諸臣之言，大抵皆以敵之彊弱為彊弱，而非以已之彊弱為彊弱
translation_en:
…among them, the benefits and harms, gains and losses also differ. Let us assess these through the affairs of the Han. Emperors Wen and Jing followed Lou Jing’s policy, sending envoys to arrange marriage alliances and securing peace on the frontier [?]. The people could work their southern fields, and the realm thereby grew prosperous: this was the effect of peace. Yet to humble the Central Kingdom in service to the barbarians was humiliating. Emperor Xiaowu, in his fury, dispatched generals, who performed the feng sacrifice at Langxu and the shan sacrifice at Guyan. The Xiongnu fled north, far beyond the frontier, and no royal court remained south of the desert: this was the effect of war. Yet to exhaust soldiers and horses in pursuing distant conquests was an abuse of military force. Crossing the Yellow River, they built walls and opened canals from Shuofang westward to Jinju [?], gradually encroaching on the northern lands, while the enemy dared not contest them: this was the effect of defense. Yet transporting grain from Shandong cost immense sums; the garrison troops saw no reduction in their numbers, and the poorer households complained of distress. This was exhausting.

Jia Yi once so resented the Xiongnu’s defiance that he shed tears at the Han court. Yet his proposed policy of the “three demonstrations and five baits” sought to bestow on them splendid clothing, carriages, music, women, lofty halls and spacious residences, storehouses, and male and female slaves. It thus proved inferior even to the annual gifts of silk: this was ill-conceived. Subsequently, Zhongshu proposed an agreement requiring a son as hostage; Anguo sought to halt the campaign at Mayi; Wei Xiang discussed warfare undertaken without a legitimate cause; and Tutor Xiao reiterated the principle of taking heed of calamity. Although their statements differed, their essential purport was merely what Ban Gu described as “the scholar-officials’ exclusive advocacy of peace through marriage alliances.” I have surveyed the affairs of that time and closely examined these ministers’ words. Broadly speaking, they all judged strength and weakness by the enemy’s strength and weakness, rather than by their own…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
者也兵法致人不致於人視敵以為強弱
則致於人矣故利害得失叅焉善乎陸贄
之言曰中夏之盛衰異勢夷狄之彊弱異
時事機之利害異情措置之安危異便形
變不同胡可專一故疆利用戰弱利用守
疆弱適均則和焉斯言也雖穰苴復生無
以易矣盖敵有疆弱吾亦有疆弱敵有盛
衰吾亦有盛衰惟能使盛疆之勢常在於
我則料敵觀變操縱有餘且戎馬之足時
===
去時来禽獸之心乍嗔乍喜堂堂中國不
必視以重輕吾將良而兵勁食足而備完
則此三策者隨其去來喜怒而應之和可
也戰可也守可也寓戰於守寓守於和亦
可也不然齎空橐而戰戰可克乎畫空城
而守守可固乎抱空約而和和可久乎知
乎此可以論今日之勢矣
天子明聖方內輯和航浮索引之國日域月窟
之民贄方物稱外臣者以千百數乃北虜
banxin: 癸丑會試錄文　五十一
alt_text:

則致於人矣故利害得失系焉善乎陸贄
之言曰中夏之盛衰異勢夷狄之強弱異
時事機之利害異情措置之安危異便形
變不同胡可專一故彊利用戰弱利用守
彊弱適均則和焉斯言也雖穰苴復生無
以易矣蓋敵有彊弱吾亦有彊弱敵有盛
衰吾亦有盛衰惟能使盛彊之勢常在於
我則將欲觀變渙然有餘且戎馬之足時
===
去時來禽獸之心作嗔乍喜豈堂堂中國不
必視以重輕吾將良而兵勁食足而備完
則此三策者隨其去來喜怒而應之和可
也戰可也守可也寓戰於守寓守於和亦
可也不然齎空橐而戰戰可克乎畫空城
而守守可固乎抱空約而和和可久乎知
乎此可以論今日之勢矣
天子明聖方內輯和航浮索引之國日域月窟
之民贄方物稱外臣者以千百數乃北虜
punctuated:
者也。兵法：「致人，不致於人。」視敵以為強弱，則致於人矣，故利害得失叅焉。善乎陸贄之言曰：「中夏之盛衰異勢，夷狄之彊弱異時，事機之利害異情，措置之安危異便，形變不同，胡可專一？故疆利用戰，弱利用守，疆弱適均則和焉。」斯言也，雖穰苴復生，無以易矣。盖敵有疆弱，吾亦有疆弱；敵有盛衰，吾亦有盛衰。惟能使盛疆之勢常在於我，則料敵觀變，操縱有餘。且戎馬之足，時去時来；禽獸之心，乍嗔乍喜。堂堂中國，不必視以重輕。吾將良而兵勁，食足而備完，則此三策者，隨其去來喜怒而應之，和可也，戰可也，守可也，寓戰於守，寓守於和，亦可也。不然，齎空橐而戰，戰可克乎？畫空城而守，守可固乎？抱空約而和，和可久乎？知乎此，可以論今日之勢矣。
天子明聖，方內輯和，航浮索引之國、日域月窟之民，贄方物、稱外臣者，以千百數。乃北虜
translation_en:
…such were they. The Art of War says: “Make others come to you; do not be made to go to others.” If we determine our strength or weakness by looking to the enemy, we are being directed by others; hence advantage and harm, success and failure, become intermingled. How well Lu Zhi put it: “The flourishing and decline of the Central Xia entail different configurations of power; the strength and weakness of the foreign peoples vary with the times. Advantage and harm in unfolding affairs depend on differing circumstances; safety and danger in the measures adopted depend on what suits each situation. Conditions change and differ: how can one adhere exclusively to a single course? Thus, when strong, it is advantageous to fight; when weak, to defend; when strengths are evenly matched, to make peace.” Even if Rangju were restored to life, he could not improve upon these words. For the enemy has strengths and weaknesses, and so do we; the enemy flourishes and declines, and so do we. Only by ensuring that prosperity and strength remain continually on our side can we assess the enemy, observe changes, and have ample scope to tighten or relax our control.
Moreover, their warhorses come and go, while their beastlike hearts shift suddenly between anger and delight. Our majestic Central Kingdom need not let its own importance depend on them. If our generals are capable and our troops strong, our provisions sufficient and our preparations complete, then we may employ these three strategies in response to their coming and going, delight and anger. Peace is acceptable, war is acceptable, and defense is acceptable; incorporating warfare into defense, or defense into peace, is also acceptable. Otherwise, if we go to war carrying empty sacks, can we win? If we defend an empty city merely drawn on paper, can our defense hold firm? If we make peace by clinging to an empty agreement, can that peace endure? Understanding this, we may discuss the circumstances of the present day.
The Son of Heaven is enlightened and sagely, and all within the realm is united in harmony. Countries reached by ships or by passage along ropes [?], and peoples from the sun’s domain to the moon’s cavern—the farthest east and west—present their local products and profess themselves outer subjects, numbering in the hundreds and thousands. Yet the northern barbarians…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
素號驕悍者今亦回面舉踵稱臣欵塞而
請
命焉盖古英君猛將所以駘藉生靈殫身百戰
而不能得者執事謂
聖德遠被非前代和議之比愚亦以為然也抑
聞道路其言有兩端尚撫綏者則曰夫越
裳南獻楛矢東来盛王之遠畧也今外叛
者已誅而内降者不聴猝有騷動其曲在
我許之便核情偽者則曰夫頡利劫盟女
===
直背約前事之殷鑒也夷虜之性叛服不
常矧物力方虛既以養兵又以資虜是重
困也勿許便夫此二說者愚以為無全是
亦無全非何也今之虜勢盖在冒頓呼韓
之間非甚彊也非甚弱也彊不如冒頓即
一旦渝盟棄好未足為中國大憂故持議
勿許者逆詐之偏指非通論也弱不如呼
韓即一旦稽顙屈膝未可謂中國無事故
持議許之者應變之權宜非完策也今方

punctuated: 素號驕悍者，今亦回面舉踵，稱臣欵塞而請命焉。盖古英君猛將所以駘藉生靈、殫身百戰而不能得者，執事謂聖德遠被，非前代和議之比，愚亦以為然也。抑聞道路，其言有兩端。尚撫綏者則曰：「夫越裳南獻，楛矢東来，盛王之遠畧也。今外叛者已誅，而内降者不聴，猝有騷動，其曲在我，許之便。」核情偽者則曰：「夫頡利劫盟，女直背約，前事之殷鑒也。夷虜之性，叛服不常。矧物力方虛，既以養兵，又以資虜，是重困也，勿許便。」夫此二說者，愚以為無全是，亦無全非。何也？今之虜勢，盖在冒頓、呼韓之間，非甚彊也，非甚弱也。彊不如冒頓，即一旦渝盟棄好，未足為中國大憂，故持議勿許者，逆詐之偏指，非通論也。弱不如呼韓，即一旦稽顙屈膝，未可謂中國無事，故持議許之者，應變之權宜，非完策也。今方
translation_en: …long reputed to be arrogant and fierce, now likewise turn toward us and hasten forward, professing themselves subjects, approaching the frontier passes, and requesting the Emperor’s commands. This is what the heroic rulers and mighty generals of antiquity could not obtain, though they trampled living souls underfoot and exhausted themselves in a hundred battles. You say that the Emperor’s sagely virtue reaches far abroad, and that this is unlike the peace negotiations of earlier dynasties. I too believe this to be so. Yet I hear two views circulating among the public. Those who favor pacification say: “Yueshang brought tribute from the south, and arrows of thornwood came from the east: such was the far-reaching statecraft of flourishing sage kings. Now that those who rebelled beyond our borders have been executed, if we refuse to hear those who submit to our authority, and unrest suddenly arises, the fault will lie with us. It is expedient to grant their request.” Those who scrutinize sincerity and deceit say: “Jieli’s coercion of a covenant and the Jurchens’ breach of their agreement are salutary warnings from the past. By their nature, these foreign enemies alternate unpredictably between rebellion and submission. Moreover, our material resources are now depleted. To use them both to maintain our troops and to supply the enemy would compound our distress. It is expedient to refuse.” Neither of these two views, I believe, is wholly right or wholly wrong. Why? The present strength of the enemy lies somewhere between that of Maodun and Huhan: they are neither exceedingly strong nor exceedingly weak. Their strength does not equal Maodun’s, so even if they should one day break the covenant and abandon friendly relations, they would not constitute a grave threat to China. Thus, those who advocate refusal offer a one-sided argument based on anticipating deception, rather than a comprehensive assessment. Nor are they as weak as Huhan, so even if they should one day bow their foreheads to the ground and bend their knees, we could not say that China would be free of trouble. Thus, those who advocate acceptance offer a temporary expedient for responding to changing circumstances, rather than a complete strategy. Now, the regional…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
鎮之臣與虜接境通譯而言能審知其嚮
義果誠設約果信乎能伛首受戎索無衆
入爭市乎縣道續食及禮賓一接之外無
他求乎民無姦闌出物乎如是則
天子何惜階前尋丈之地使者盈尺之紙隔閡
夷情狹小
皇化愚亦曰許之可矣夫許之可也許之而遂
弛吾中國之防不可也何者今虜雖內順
而諸邊戍卒非減也司農藏錢粟以日月
===
銖兩責辨歲額不能省也近塞磽瘠之地
又非能卒卒開種也而兵以益驕吏以益
狎則天下之患豈必在虜易曰其亡其亡
繫于苞桑書曰惟事事乃其有備有備無
患此皆憂危之論老成之見也蓋昔者渾

進諫請收鹵胡人以賜從軍死事者家竟

他求乎民無敢闌出物乎如是則
天子何惜階前尋丈之地使者盈尺之紙關
夷情狹小
皇化愚亦曰許之可矣夫許之可也許之而遂

translation_en:
…the officials commanding the frontier garrisons border on the enemy and communicate with them through interpreters. Can they ascertain that their inclination toward righteousness is truly sincere and that they will truly keep the agreements they make? Can the enemy bow their heads and accept military regulations, without entering in crowds to contend for trade at the markets? Beyond provisions supplied along the way by the counties and a single reception with the courtesies due to guests, will they make no further demands? Will there be no dishonest people illicitly taking goods across the frontier? If so, why should the Son of Heaven begrudge a few feet of ground before his steps or a foot-long sheet of paper for an envoy, thereby obstructing the expression of the foreigners’ sentiments and restricting the reach of imperial transformation? I too would say that granting their request is acceptable.

But although granting it is acceptable, granting it and consequently relaxing the defenses of our Central Realm is not. Why? Although the enemy now submits, the soldiers garrisoning the various frontiers have not been reduced. The Chamberlain for National Treasury stores money and grain, requiring their provision by the day and month, down to the smallest weights; the annual quotas cannot be reduced. Nor can the poor, barren lands near the frontier be brought under cultivation in haste. If the soldiers consequently grow more arrogant and the officials more negligent, must the troubles of the realm necessarily come from the enemy?

The Book of Changes says: “It may perish! It may perish! Bind it to a clump of mulberry trees.” The Book of Documents says: “Only by attending to every affair can there be preparedness; with preparedness there is no calamity.” These are all words of concern about danger, the judgments of mature experience.

Formerly, when Hunye submitted, Emperor Wu of Han considered executing the merchants who had traded with the enemy. Ji An indignantly remonstrated, requesting that the Hu people be seized as captives and bestowed upon the families of those who had died on military service. During the Jingning era, the chanyu submitted a memorial requesting the abolition of frontier defenses to give rest to the Son of Heaven’s people. Hou Ying, a Gentleman of the Palace, set forth ten harmful consequences of doing so. Now, the principal aim of Ji An’s impassioned words was …

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
全護根本而應則為國家憂將然逆未形
自古言和戎利害莫切於此今日之勢雖
萬無妆鹵降胡之理亦宜稍倣二臣之意
撫安人民以内固其根本而嚴飭將吏以
外修守戰之具督屯募農鍛甲厲刃嚴柝
遠堠增墉浚濠使元氣不泄於鍼芒河隄
不潰於蟻穴倘可少紓執事之憂乎大抵
戰守和三策也而守常居戰與和之中能
守則可以和可以無和能守則可以戰可
===
以無戰是三策歸之一策也許與勿許二
說也而許之以迹不許之以心修守戰於
閒暇寓防禦於羈縻是二說歸之一說可
也此愚前之所謂審盛衰彊弱之勢致人
而不致於人者也何休曰王者不治夷狄
來者不拒去者勿追而蘇氏非之曰聖王
於夷狄吾欲其來則來之不可得而去也
吾欲其去則拒之不可得而來也今能使
制和者在中國而不在夷狄則吾之力常

punctuated: 全護根本，而應則為國家憂將然、逆未形。自古言和戎利害，莫切於此。今日之勢，雖萬無妆鹵降胡之理，亦宜稍倣二臣之意，撫安人民，以内固其根本；而嚴飭將吏，以外修守戰之具。督屯募農，鍛甲厲刃，嚴柝遠堠，增墉浚濠，使元氣不泄於鍼芒，河隄不潰於蟻穴，倘可少紓執事之憂乎？大抵戰、守、和三策也，而守常居戰與和之中。能守則可以和，可以無和；能守則可以戰，可以無戰。是三策歸之一策也。許與勿許二說也，而許之以迹，不許之以心，修守戰於閒暇，寓防禦於羈縻，是二說歸之一說可也。此愚前之所謂審盛衰彊弱之勢，致人而不致於人者也。何休曰：「王者不治夷狄，來者不拒，去者勿追。」而蘇氏非之曰：「聖王於夷狄，吾欲其來則來之，不可得而去也；吾欲其去則拒之，不可得而來也。」今能使制和者在中國，而不在夷狄，則吾之力常
translation_en:
…to preserve and protect the foundations, whereas Ying anticipated impending dangers to the state and forestalled troubles before they took shape. Of all discussions since antiquity of the benefits and harms of making peace with the Rong, none is more pertinent than these. Under present circumstances, although there is absolutely no prospect of taking captives and receiving the submission of the Hu [?], we should still follow something of these two ministers’ intentions: soothe and secure the people, thereby strengthening our foundations within, and strictly admonish commanders and officials, thereby preparing the means of defense and warfare without. Supervise military agricultural colonies and recruit farmers; forge armor and sharpen blades; maintain strict night watches and extend the network of watchposts; heighten walls and deepen moats. Ensure that our vital energy does not escape through a pinprick, nor a river dike collapse through an anthole. Might this somewhat ease your concerns?
Broadly speaking, there are three policies: war, defense, and peace. Defense always stands between war and peace. If we can defend ourselves, we may make peace or dispense with peace; if we can defend ourselves, we may fight or dispense with fighting. Thus the three policies resolve into one. There are two positions: to grant the request or not to grant it. Yet we may grant it outwardly without assenting inwardly, prepare for defense and warfare in times of leisure, and embed defensive measures within a policy of loose rein. In this way, the two positions may properly resolve into one. This is what I meant earlier by assessing the balance of flourishing and decline, strength and weakness, and making others come at our bidding rather than going at theirs.
He Xiu said: “The true king does not govern the Yi and Di. Those who come are not turned away; those who leave are not pursued.” But Master Su criticized this, saying: “In dealing with the Yi and Di, the sage king brings them in when he wishes them to come, so that they cannot leave; when he wishes them to go, he keeps them out, so that they cannot come.” If we can now ensure that control over peace rests with the Central Kingdom rather than with the Yi and Di, then our strength will always…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
有餘而許與不許不足論矣雖然此邊吏
之事也抑聞揆影者植表防川者塞源理
身者先榮衞制勝者在朝廷夫
朝廷之事愚何足以知之哉然竊見比者文
墨議論多於功實循習玩愒多於忠計守
令鮮循良之績閭里興愁歎之聲則執事
所謂外寧內憂意其在此夫惟
天子當饋拊髀考朝序夕徹桑土於未雨戒衣
袽於終日而公卿百僚相與挈持綱維修
===
輔德業無飾文貌無苟目前虞周太平之
理可幾而睹也

punctuated: 有餘，而許與不許不足論矣。雖然，此邊吏之事也。抑聞揆影者植表，防川者塞源，理身者先榮衞，制勝者在朝廷。夫朝廷之事，愚何足以知之哉？然竊見比者，文墨議論多於功實，循習玩愒多於忠計，守令鮮循良之績，閭里興愁歎之聲，則執事所謂外寧內憂，意其在此。夫惟天子當饋拊髀，考朝序夕，徹桑土於未雨，戒衣袽於終日，而公卿百僚相與挈持綱維，修輔德業，無飾文貌，無苟目前，虞周太平之理，可幾而睹也。
translation_en:
…will always be more than sufficient, and whether to grant or withhold consent will scarcely merit discussion. Even so, these are matters for frontier officials. Yet I have heard that those who measure shadows erect a gnomon; those who guard against flooding dam the source; those who care for the body attend first to its nutritive and protective vital energies; and the power to secure victory lies with the court. As for the court’s affairs, how could someone as foolish as I presume to understand them? Nevertheless, I have privately observed that lately literary argument has outweighed actual accomplishment, and habitual complacency and idle delay have outweighed loyal counsel. Prefects and magistrates have few achievements in benevolent administration, while the sounds of sorrow and lament rise from the villages. I suspect that herein lies what you, sir, call tranquility abroad and anxiety within.

If only the Son of Heaven would slap his thigh while at his meal in longing for worthy men, review and order affairs morning and evening [?], gather mulberry roots before the rain to secure the nest, and remain mindful all day of keeping rags ready to stop a boat’s leaks; and if the highest ministers and all the officials would together uphold the governing framework and cultivate and further his virtue and achievements, neither embellishing outward appearances nor seeking merely to get by for the moment—then we might hope to witness the peaceful governance of the ages of Yu and Zhou.

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Metropolitan Examination

In the second month of spring this year, scholars from throughout the realm awaited examination at the Ministry of Rites. The ministry’s officials petitioned the throne concerning the matter. His Majesty commanded Grand Secretary Juzheng to oversee the work, with your servant Diaoyang as his deputy. On the day of our farewell audience, His Majesty, taking advantage of the mild spring weather, was attending the Classics Colloquium and the Daily Lecture. Your servant was then serving in rotation at both, and was dispatched from the curtained imperial quarters. Once the scholars had been selected and a record compiled, your servant respectfully composed this postface for its closing pages.

Your servant reflects that a tree a thousand chi tall does not grow in a single year, nor is a thousand chi of fine silk woven in a single day. So too with scholars. Confucius, praising the ancient rulers Yao and Shun, said: “At the juncture of Tang and Yu, talent flourished most abundantly.” Indeed, at that transition between Tang and Yu, successive ages of brilliance and accumulated…

皇考肅皇帝綱紀作人多□
則今日人才之衆盛□

translation_en:
…harmony, and only then did the recruitment of worthy men reach its exceptional flourishing. Indeed [?], this was not the work of a single day or night.
Our dynasty’s government and instruction have been excellent and enlightened, and its moral influence has flourished for a hundred years. Our imperial father, the revered Emperor Su, established order and nurtured men of talent in many □ ways [?]; thus the abundance of talented men today □ [?].
We reverently reflect that His Majesty has succeeded to the imperial enterprise and established the supreme standard, honoring the Way and esteeming literary learning. From the inauguration of the Longqing era, ding [the date is garbled], to the xinwei year [1571], five years have elapsed, and the Provincial and Metropolitan Examinations have been held four times in all. Now he has again approved the remonstrance officials’ request to increase the quota of metropolitan graduates (jinshi). His desire to seek worthy men to assist in governing is profoundly earnest and sincere…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
之出責乎出責者必質券焉
信然雖質券矣而信者蓋寡
臣懼士之負責而背券者多
也雖然此臣愚慮之過也雷
霆必發潛底震動枹鼓鏗鉤
介士奮竦是故聖人南面而
立號令未施而天下延頸舉
===
踵以向之者精誠之所通也
上以誠求士矣士有不以誠應之
者耶
皇上至德昭孚感召神速臣嘗竊
伏覩識而知其然也往者雨
澤愆期農事未遂
聖心軫矣雩禱方興而靈澍即霈

踵以向之者精誠之所通也
===
上以誠求士矣士有不以誠應之
者耶
皇上至德昭孚感召神速臣嘗竊
伏覩識而知其然也往者雨
澤愆期農事未遂
聖心軫念雩禱方興而靈澍即霈
punctuated:
之出責，乎出責者必質券焉。信然，雖質券矣，而信者蓋寡。臣懼士之負責而背券者多也。雖然，此臣愚慮之過也。雷霆必發，潛底震動；枹鼓鏗鉤，介士奮竦。是故聖人南面而立，號令未施，而天下延頸舉踵以向之者，精誠之所通也。上以誠求士矣，士有不以誠應之者耶？
皇上至德昭孚，感召神速，臣嘗竊伏覩識而知其然也。往者雨澤愆期，農事未遂，聖心軫矣，雩禱方興，而靈澍即霈。
translation_en:
…lending [?]; those who lend must require a bond as security. Indeed, even with a bond as security, those who keep faith are few. Your servant fears that many scholars will incur this debt yet violate their bond. Nevertheless, this is excessive anxiety on the part of your foolish servant. When thunder breaks forth, those hidden in the depths tremble; when drumsticks strike and drums resound [?], armored warriors spring to attention. Thus, when the sage stands facing south, even before his commands have been issued, all under Heaven crane their necks and rise on tiptoe to turn toward him: such is the penetrating power of utmost sincerity. Your Majesty has sought scholars with sincerity; could any scholar fail to respond with sincerity?
Your Majesty’s supreme virtue is manifest and inspires trust; its power to move and summon responses is wondrously swift. Your servant has respectfully observed and taken note of this, and knows it to be so. Previously, when the rains were overdue and farming could not proceed to completion, Your Majesty’s sagely heart was troubled. The rain rites and prayers had scarcely begun when the blessed rain poured down.

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
又如
郊禋孔嚴
乘輿夙駕則陰曀潜消塵清
輦道又如邊書告急
廟筭爲厪則名王輸欵乞貢求封
是幽而
天道遠而夷狄感召神速若聲之
===
於呼而影之於歩也况凡民
之秀者乎爾諸士遘遇
明時報答
主德則將何以亦曰
上以誠求之下以誠應之耳信爾
言不易爾行敦爾節不易爾
守誠也誠則可貴可賤可遠

===
於呼而影之於步也況凡民
之秀者乎爾諸士遭遇
明時報答
主德則將何以亦曰
上以誠求之下以誠應之耳信爾
言不易爾行敦爾節不易爾
守誠也誠則可貴可賤可遠
punctuated: 又如郊禋孔嚴，乘輿夙駕，則陰曀潜消，塵清輦道；又如邊書告急，廟筭爲厪，則名王輸欵，乞貢求封。是幽而天道，遠而夷狄，感召神速，若聲之於呼而影之於歩也，况凡民之秀者乎？爾諸士遘遇明時，報答主德，則將何以？亦曰：上以誠求之，下以誠應之耳。信爾言，不易爾行；敦爾節，不易爾守，誠也。誠則可貴可賤可遠
translation_en:
…Again, when the suburban sacrifice to Heaven was conducted with utmost solemnity and the imperial carriage set out early, the overcast skies quietly cleared, and dust vanished from the imperial route. Again, when dispatches from the frontier reported an emergency and plans for its defense weighed upon the court, renowned kings offered their allegiance, requesting permission to present tribute and seeking investiture. Thus, even the hidden Way of Heaven and the distant non-Chinese peoples respond to the imperial influence with miraculous speed, like an echo answering a call or a shadow following a step. How much more, then, should the finest among the common people respond!

You scholars have had the good fortune to encounter an enlightened age. How, then, will you repay your sovereign’s virtue? It is simply this: those above seek men with sincerity, and those below respond with sincerity. Be trustworthy in your words and unswerving in your conduct; strengthen your integrity and do not alter the principles you uphold. This is sincerity. With sincerity, you may be honored, you may be treated as lowly, you may be kept at a distance…

title: 隆慶五年會試錄
text:
可近而不可奪志矣
見染者而嘆曰嘻入
蒼也入乎黄而黄也
變於入者皆質未定
士前定乎誠矣猶之□
也不可奪堅丹可磨
奪赤又何所入之足□
===
哉多士勉於誠而已
通議大夫吏部左侍□
林院學士掌詹事府□
陽謹序

===

通議大夫吏部左侍郎
林院學士掌詹事府□
陽謹序
punctuated:
可近，而不可奪志矣。見染者而嘆曰：「嘻！入蒼也，入乎黄而黄也。」變於入者，皆質未定。士前定乎誠矣，猶之□也，不可奪堅；丹可磨，奪赤，又何所入之足□哉？多士勉於誠而已。

通議大夫、吏部左侍□、林院學士、掌詹事府□陽謹序。
translation_en:
…may be drawn near, yet cannot be deprived of their resolve. Seeing those engaged in dyeing, he sighed: “Alas! Entering blue [?]; entering yellow, it becomes yellow.” Those changed by what they enter all lack a settled essential character. Once a scholar has grounded himself firmly in sincerity, he is like □, whose hardness cannot be taken away. Cinnabar may be ground, [but can it be] deprived of its redness [?]? How, then, could whatever he enters suffice to □? You many scholars need only strive for sincerity.
